condition.label: hypermobility spectrum disorder
condition.distinctions: HSD is symptomatic hypermobility after differential diagnosis,not asymptomatic flexibility or all Ehlers-Danlos syndromes. Trial enrolled no hEDS despite protocol allowing it.

sources.title: Short-term effectiveness of high-load compared with low-load strengthening exercise on self-reported function in patients with hypermobile shoulders: a randomised controlled trial

access.details: Complete Europe PMC XML retrieved; eligibility, actual intervention, Tables 2/3 and limitations inspected. None of 100 participants had hEDS.

integrity.method: Inspected primary article metadata/version and linked notices; Crossref DOI works metadata request and focused later-evidence searches on 2026-11-01. Not a registry-wide clearance.
integrity.result: Crossref lookup returned HTTP Error 429: Too Many Requests; no complete external registry check. No notice identified in the retrieved article text; absence not established.

sources.design: Assessor-blinded randomized trial of 100 adults; 93 completed 16-week assessment. Supervision/contact differed substantially.
sources.population: Generalized or historical HSD, age 18–65, shoulder pain/instability at least 3 months; 79% women, mean age 37.8. No hEDS enrolled. Shoulder surgery within 1 year and injection within 3 months excluded.
sources.comparator: LIGHT: nine posture/isometric exercises progressing to yellow-band dynamic home training three times weekly; introduction plus supervision at weeks 5 and 11.
sources.coInterventions: Both groups received scapular correction/joint protection education; concomitant manual therapy/injections discouraged and recorded.
sources.outcomes: At 16 weeks, WOSI adjusted between-group difference −174.5/2100 (95% CI −341.4 to −7.7), 8.3%, below the predefined minimal important difference. Most secondary outcomes inconclusive; NNT 7 (95% CI 4–620) very imprecise.
sources.followUp: 16 weeks; later one-year report uses the same cohort.
sources.uncertainty: Participants and therapists unblinded; attention/supervision differed; group mean difference below MID; individual exercises not tested separately.
sources.harms: No serious adverse events; HEAVY muscle soreness 56% versus 37%, headache 40% versus 20%. Two HEAVY withdrawals due to adverse events. Table 3 includes one dislocation in HEAVY versus zero LIGHT; events were not necessarily caused by intervention.
sources.limitations: Cannot generalize to all joints, hEDS, postoperative shoulders, unsupervised loading or unrestricted end range.

protocol.execution: Five dumbbell exercises: side-lying external rotation in neutral, prone horizontal abduction, prone external rotation at 90° abduction, supine protraction, seated scaption.
protocol.dose: Five-minute unloaded warm-up. Weeks 1–3: 3×10 at 50%, 70%, 90% of 10RM; weeks 4–9: 3×10RM; weeks 10–15: 4×8RM; week 16 taper.
protocol.supervision: Two individual physiotherapist sessions plus one home session weekly. Relative load estimated from 5RM test; high relative effort does not necessarily mean high kilograms.
protocol.progression: Individual load adjustment; protocol/manual define quality criteria and contain timing discrepancies.
protocol.stoppingRules: Study allowed acceptable symptoms below 5/10. Detailed modification instructions in protocol/manual differ in symptom timing; not an app default.

sources.design: Prospective trial protocol and intervention manual; no independent treatment outcomes.
sources.population: Planned HSD/hEDS adults with persistent shoulder complaints; actual 2022 cohort included HSD only.
sources.comparator: LIGHT exercise plan with lower supervision.
sources.coInterventions: Shared scapular correction and joint protection education.
sources.outcomes: Defines planned execution, loading and control; does not supply an efficacy estimate.
sources.followUp: Planned 16 weeks and 1 year; actual outcomes are separate reports.
sources.uncertainty: Manual describes first 4 weeks as preparatory versus 3-week familiarisation in main protocol. Manual says pain return to baseline within 30 minutes/before next session; protocol reduces demands if symptoms persist more than 2–3 hours. Do not invent a harmonized threshold.
sources.harms: Modification/reporting plan, not observed harms; 2022 outcome paper reports events.
sources.limitations: Manual advice about back twisting, bent-back work and extreme positions is untested shared education; it is not causal evidence for universal HSD restrictions.

protocol.execution: Manual specifies side-lying external rotation with pillow between upper arm/trunk; prone horizontal arm raise with outward rotation; seated scaption; prone external rotation with supported upper arm and elbow at 90°; supported supine straight-arm protraction.
protocol.dose: Three seconds concentric plus three seconds eccentric; 3×10 with 60-second rests through week 9, then 4×8 with 90-second rests in weeks 10–16. Week 16 load is 70% of 8RM; 48 hours between sessions.
protocol.frequency: Three sessions weekly for 16 weeks: two supervised, one home.
protocol.supervision: Trained physiotherapists, same clinician where possible; individual 5RM test and movement-quality control.
protocol.progression: Increase if all sets exceed target repetitions with acceptable symptoms and good control: no glenohumeral subluxation or increased scapular dyskinesis. Full ROM was planned for HEAVY; not universal end-range clearance.
protocol.stoppingRules: Protocol reduces load, ROM, sets, repetitions, frequency or provoking exercises if symptoms persist beyond 2–3 hours; baseline resting pain above 5/10 permits no increase. Manual gives different 30-minute timing; clinical reconciliation required.

sources.design: Secondary one-year analysis of the same 100-person randomized trial; not independent replication.
sources.population: Same HSD shoulder cohort; 86% completed one-year follow-up.
sources.comparator: HEAVY versus LIGHT; postprogram activity not randomized.
sources.coInterventions: Shared education and subsequent usual care.
sources.outcomes: WOSI change: HEAVY −456.9 (95% CI −572.2 to −341.7), LIGHT −364.0 (−481.4 to −246.6); between-group difference −92.9 (−257.4 to 71.5), not significant. Clinically important improvement: 64% versus 60%.
sources.uncertainty: Secondary analysis, attrition and uncertain postprogram training; null confidence interval does not prove equivalence.
sources.harms: No new causal long-term safety clearance from this report.
sources.limitations: Short-term relative advantage does not establish sustained one-year superiority.

sources.design: Six studies, 231 participants. Authors label studies quasi-experimental while citing several randomized studies; design classification and heterogeneity limit certainty.
sources.population: Ages 7–45, mixed Brighton/Beighton diagnoses, JHS/EDS; indirect for contemporary adult HSD.
sources.outcomes: Pain effect CI −2.164 to −0.357, with high heterogeneity (I² 81.799%); strength CI −0.389 to 0.495, nonsignificant. Effects were not uniform across outcomes.
sources.uncertainty: Small mixed-age/diagnostic samples, co-interventions, inconsistent design classification and imprecision; low certainty.
sources.harms: No comprehensive adverse-event synthesis establishing universal safety.
sources.limitations: Does not establish a blanket HSD stretching/end-range ban or justify shoulder-to-knee transfer.

gaps: Independent clinical review absent. All mappings/rules/requests are candidates; no therapeutic release, clinical approval or universally safe exercise claim.
Source doses describe studied or recommended contexts, not individual app prescriptions. No generic five-second stretch progression or strength-set credit for stretching.
Coexisting conditions, equipment, independently selected joint limits and user-confirmed starting load remain separate constraints; no restriction may be relaxed to fill an empty workout.
Protocol/manual inconsistency: 3 versus 4 weeks of preparation and 30 minutes versus 2–3 hours symptom timing. Do not resolve by guessing.
No evidence here for a blanket ban on end range, stretching or heavy loading; other joint-specific restrictions still prevail.
Lower-limb synthesis does not map contemporary HSD perfectly; no exact lower-limb mappings created. PMID 41637690 is a scoping-review protocol, not results.
Five HEAVY exercise figures located and accompanying text read; figures not independently visually verified. Retained PNG creation needs real provenance and independent content review.
